title: Structured payload field shift after proxy timestamp skew
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Multiple customers using Private (VPC) deployments reported that structured JSON payloads returned by function/tool integrations intermittently have fields shifted one position to the right (e.g., 'result' appears where 'id' should be). The issue reproduces only when requests traverse the customer-managed proxy path with high clock skew/timestamp jitter. Hypothesis: an upstream timestamp header with microsecond precision interacts with our chunk reassembly heuristics, causing a mis-ordered concatenation step when a small fraction of chunks are prefetched and then re-sequenced.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a sample tool that returns a 3-field JSON object in a streaming response
2) Send requests through a proxy that appends/rewrites X-Request-Timestamp with millisecond/microsecond values
3) Enable KV cache prefetch (default on Dedicated/Private) and simulate concurrent requests at low inter-arrival times
4) Observe occasional JSON field order shifts in the reassembled payload (seen in raw streaming logs)
investigation: 2026-03-10: Initial customer report from AcmeHealth and FinEdge Ops; attached sample payloads and raw stream captures.
2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging by creating a proxy shim that injects variable X-Request-Timestamp; confirmed field-shift occurs ~0.6% of requests under stress.

2026-03-11: Core runtime logs show reassembly step treats timestamp-tokenized chunk boundaries as soft separators when prefetch buffer contains 1-2 chunks; ordering metadata (seq_id) is correct but byte-offset merge incorrectly uses header-trimmed length leading to one-field offset.
2026-03-12: Confirmed behavior only when 'stream-prefetch' enabled and 'proxy-timestamp' header length > 12 bytes; disabled prefetch eliminates the symptom.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed raw payloads (no secrets leaked).
decision: 1) Ship hotfix to reassembly: switch from heuristic-based separator detection to strict seq_id merge for streaming chunks.
2) Short-term mitigation: add server-side safeguard to detect monotonic seq_id gaps and fallback to conservative reassembly (disabled prefetch semantics) for affected tenant IDs.
3) Add telemetry and a sampled diff pipeline to detect future shifts automatically and alert on >0.1% rate.
4) Backport fix to runtime-1.26 and runtime-1.25-stable for Dedicated and Private customers.
next_steps: 2026-03-13: PR #12058 created (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12058) implementing strict seq_id merge; tests added for variable header lengths.
2026-03-13: Deploy hotfix to staging Dedicated and run long-running traffic job (12h) with proxy shim to verify fix under load.
2026-03-14: Prepare customer communications template and coordinate with CSMs for impacted tenants (AcmeHealth, FinEdge).
2026-03-15: Canaries on hosted infra for customers using Private routing; monitor new telemetry and rollback plan ready.
